header.business: A home services company (heating, cooling and plumbing)

close_rates.source: measured from the CRM export, 2025-10 to 2026-09: 1,717 jobs from 3,323 paid leads, 2,299 jobs from 3,723 unpaid leads

header.paid_cost_source: this run's Google Ads plan: 266.8 leads a month for $14,040 after the rebalance (258 results in the decision window)

headline: Plan $486,480 for 2027, 12% of the revenue target: the goal needs 3,480 paid leads, and Google Ads can buy 3,440 of them at an acceptable cost.
Paid media is $185,330 (38%); people, agencies, tools and booked events are $240,300; content is $18,000; tests get $18,530 and contingency $24,320.
40 paid leads (about $14,800 of revenue) are out of reach on Google alone: the test reserve funds the Microsoft Ads test that could close it.

from_the_goal.inputs: $2,950,000 new revenue / $720 = 4,097 customers; 2,299 from unpaid leads; 3,480 paid leads at a 51.7% close rate; paid media $185,330 + other lines $258,300 + test reserve $18,530 + contingency $24,320

benchmark_share_of_revenue.source: Gartner 2025 CMO Spend Survey (press release, May 2025)
benchmark_share_of_revenue.who_was_surveyed: 402 CMOs and marketing leaders in North America, the UK and Europe, most at companies with more than $1 billion in revenue

last_12_months.inputs: people $168,000, agencies $36,000, tools $9,600, content $14,400, events $18,000, paid media $162,580 (Google Ads, 2025-10 to 2026-09)

why: The goal needs 7,203 leads against 7,046 last year, and paid growth past today's level costs $66.67 to $75.00 a lead at the margin, against $52.62 on average today.

The benchmark describes mostly companies with more than $1 billion in revenue, which spread people and tools over far more sales; for a local service business it is a floor to sanity-check against, not a target.

The goal total is 19% above last year: $77,900, of which $22,750 is paid media, $42,850 is the test reserve and contingency that last year didn't have, and the rest is raises, the tool price rise, more content and the booked shows.
total_three_ways.why_this_one: the goal total: both close rates rest on more than 30 jobs and the paid cost on more than 30 results

months.first_month_note: January's paid media is $20,180 against today's $14,040 run rate: a move of more than 25%, so it goes in weekly rollout steps.

rules_for_moving_money: Review plan against actual every month; money moves only at that review.
Underspend: a flexible line under 85% of its month two months running hands the unspent part to contingency (for paid media in an average month: under $13,130).

Contingency ($24,320) is released only for a paid line that passed its gate and still has headroom, a month whose jobs run 20% or more above its index, or an approved overrun on a fixed line; each release names its trigger and who approved it.
Inside paid media, money moves by the rebalancing triggers and the weekly rollout steps.
No flexible line moves more than 20% of its annual amount in a quarter without rerunning the total (paid media: $37,070; content: $3,600); fixed lines don't move mid-year.
Every quarter, recompute the total with actual close rates and costs; if it moves more than 10%, re-phase the remaining months.
In the last quarter, unspent contingency goes to the paid line with the lowest marginal cost that has headroom, or back to the business, as the budget owner chooses.
